verdict: REJECT as a rate lever (owner rule: < 1% per-user gain after composition; control also fails the 1.2 GHz SS screen); code stays opt-in on main, the super-block layout and the adopted gather (ot_hdc_v41x_idx_kgather) remain the baseline

ninety_percent_rule.why: a rank's gather is ~9.2K sectors of ~512 random 8-key blocks (4 x ~130 a stack, ~4 a pseudo-channel): row layout bound (block = 17 reads on one bank group, tCCD_L 2.56 ns) = 261 cycles = 34% of peak; channel balance of ANY static block->channel map on these lists <= 77% (sector-granular spreading, which is ACT/tFAW-bound) -- 90% is not reachable for this load

full_scan_decision: scanned layers (L2/L8/L14/L20) keep the super-block layout (92-94%, results/rtl/dsrom_1m_measured_20261004/reader.json); the row layout scans below 90% under the controller's per-bank refresh

dram_check.timing_runs_violations: 0 on every real-list gather and every scan; 1 in the functional 2,048-block case (func_full_list_2048_p1), the same REFpb rule below
dram_check.roundtrip_violations: 90 over the five write->read runs (each ~73K-cycle write phase), all the REFpb rule below
dram_check.roundtrip_rule: REFpb during the bank's refresh: the controller model (ot_hdc_v41x_idx_hbm, REFPB 3) can refresh the same bank twice < tRFCpb apart across a 32-REFpb set boundary in long runs; pre-existing, independent of the layout
dram_check.tRREFD: not a rule of the controller model; counted: row-layout gathers 43-69 a run vs 595-735 for the super-block gather

composition.basis: candidate_gather variant: re-index index read = the ROW-LAYOUT gather (worst rank of the real 1M lists, both placements) and the select on its RTL beat stream; previous = the super-block gather

screen.worst: per-channel issuer (round-robin over 16 entries + same-bank wait)

capacity: row layout: 128 B a key instead of 68 B; re-index layers at 1M +240 MiB a user (+15 MiB a stack)
